newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open softer, upside capped.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open softer, upside capped.

text.p: Singapore shares took a breather at mid-morning on Wednesday from recent rallies and opened a tad softer following a slight drop in Wall Street, dealers said.
"Some of the blue-chips have eased slightly but I won't say there is a sell-off," a dealer with a local bank said.
"On the other hand, There is no reason for this market to rise any further. Most (players) are waiting for a clearer direction from Wall Street and the Fed," he said.
At 0230 GMT, the key Straits Times Industrials Index was down 12.21 points, at 2,176.84.
Total market volume was light, at 34.5 million shares with losers leading gainers at 104 to 47.
Leading the losers were Fraser & Neave and City Development Ltd, shedding Singapore $0.40 (US$0.28) and S$0.20 respectively.
SIA Foreign and UOB Ltd led the gainers, rising $0.20 and $0.10 respectively to S$14.60 and S$8.60.
SingTel continued to lead the actives with 2.4 million shares, of which 1.5 million were blocked at S$3.187 and $3.208.
Rashid Hussain, also among the actives, saw 1.9 million shares blocked at S$6.75, dealers said.
